system_prompt: You are a careful game QA test designer. Return ONLY valid JSON. Generate executable test specifications, not test results. Never claim a test passed. SCOPE: CONTROLS ONLY. You test whether each player control works, NOT whether the game can be won, scored, lost or completed. Work in two steps. STEP 1: read the play manual and plan and list every player control (a key the player presses), what it does, and the exact console line the manual says the game prints when it takes effect. STEP 2: write exactly one test per control: start the game, wait if the control needs a moment to be valid, press that key, wait about 1 second, and expect that exact console line. Do not test game mechanics, scoring, collisions, enemies, win/lose conditions, visuals or level completion: leave those requirements out entirely.

files.purpose: Marks the game directory as a Python package.
Main game logic, Pygame setup, game loop, event handling, and rendering.
Defines the Snake class, handling its movement, growth, and collision detection.
Defines the Food class, handling its position and spawning.
Stores game constants like grid size, colors, and speeds.

assets.strategy_rationale: The spec explicitly states 'Use plain coloured squares only; no images or sounds.', so all graphics will be drawn procedurally.

grid_system.detail: The game operates on a discrete 20x20 grid. All positions for the snake and food are integer coordinates within this grid. Rendering will scale these grid coordinates to pixel positions on the screen.

architecture.test_input_example: Press RIGHT for 5 seconds, then UP for 2 seconds, then LEFT for 3 seconds, then DOWN for 2 seconds. Repeat until game over. Press R to restart. Press ESC to quit.

play_manual.test_input: Press RIGHT for 5 seconds, then UP for 2 seconds, then LEFT for 3 seconds, then DOWN for 2 seconds. Repeat until game over. Press R to restart. Press ESC to quit.
play_manual.expected_lose_output: Console prints: GAME OVER (when collision happens). Console also prints SCORE:<n> as score increases and RESTART on new game and QUIT on exit. On-screen: 'GAME OVER - Final Score: <n>' is displayed in the middle of the grid HUD area when game ends.
play_manual.notes:
Controls and exact console lines:
- Arrow keys: when a new direction is accepted prints 'DIRECTION <UP|DOWN|LEFT|RIGHT>' (only printed when direction actually changes and not when reversing).
- Eating food: prints 'SCORE:<n>' (n is new score). HUD shows Score: <n> at top of window.
- Restart: pressing 'R' prints 'RESTART' and resets snake and score to 0.
- Quit: pressing Escape or closing the window prints 'QUIT' and exits.
- Game over: collision with wall or self prints 'GAME OVER' and displays 'GAME OVER - Final Score: <n>' on screen. The snake stops moving until 'R' is pressed.

Implementation notes and mapping to source files:
- Grid (20x20), rendering, HUD, input handling, main loop, and prints: game/snake_game.py
- Snake model, movement, growth, and collision helpers: game/snake.py
- Food spawning and position: game/food.py
- Constants (grid size, cell size, colors, FPS): game/constants.py

Known limitations / approximations:
- No audio or external assets used, per Plan. All graphics are solid filled rectangles.
- The game prints 'RESTART' on startup because new_game() is called during initialization. This is intentional and documented.
- Movement is frame-based at FPS=10 as required; speed changes by adjusting FPS in constants.

Exact runtime controls to test manually: Hold arrow keys or press them; movement is continuous at 10 FPS. Use R to restart and Esc to quit.

controls.manual_quote: the exact manual sentence that states this key and its printed line

observation.target: the console line the play manual says this control prints

generation_notes: which controls were found, and any control that could not be tested and why

constraints: Fill 'controls' first (STEP 1), then 'tests' (STEP 2). One test per control, test_ids C01, C02, ...
Only list a control if the play manual names the key AND the exact console line it prints. Put the supporting manual sentence in manual_quote. Never invent a printed line.
Each test's 'expected' must be exactly the control's 'prints' line, and observation.method must be stdout.
For a terminal (text) game a control is a typed command: use {"type": "input", "text": "go north"} (the validator adds the Enter) and put the command in the control's key field.

Actions: press / key_down / key_up / wait (and input for terminal games) only. Key names are pyautogui names: up, down, left, right, space, enter, esc, and single letters (r, w, a, s, d...). A wait uses 'seconds' (max 30).

If the manual says a control only works in a certain state (e.g. R only after game over, jump only when on the ground), add the inputs/waits needed to reach that state first. If that state cannot be reached reliably with simple inputs, mark the test not_testable and say why.
Set requirement_index to the plan requirement that mentions this control (zero-based); if none fits, use 0.
Do not write code, do not invent script_path values (use null), and do not add tests for anything other than controls.
